buyer_question: We want to use schedule for in-process periodic jobs in a service we will run for years — is the project's CI actually green, are the dependency-free and Python-version claims still true, and do the README examples run?

claims.text: The package 'schedule' can be installed from PyPI with `pip install schedule`, after which `import schedule` succeeds.
claims.probe_hint: python3 -m venv /tmp/v && /tmp/v/bin/pip install schedule && /tmp/v/bin/python -c 'import schedule; print(schedule.__version__)'

claims.text: The 'schedule' package is tested on Python 3.7, 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12.
claims.probe_hint: gh api 'repos/dbader/schedule/contents/.github/workflows/ci.yml' --jq .content | base64 -d | grep -A8 'python-version'; gh api 'repos/dbader/schedule/actions/runs?per_page=3' --jq '.workflow_runs[] | "\(.conclusion) \(.created_at)"'

claims.text: The schedule README's GitHub Actions 'Tests' badge asserts that the Tests workflow on dbader/schedule master is currently passing.
The 'schedule' package is very lightweight and has no external dependencies (installing it pulls in no other packages).
claims.source_quote: - Very lightweight and no external dependencies.
claims.probe_hint: python3 -m venv /tmp/v && /tmp/v/bin/pip install schedule && /tmp/v/bin/pip freeze | grep -v schedule | wc -l  # expect 0

claims.text: In Python with 'schedule' installed, `schedule.every(10).seconds.do(job)` (where job is any callable) registers a job without raising.
In Python with 'schedule' installed, `schedule.every().day.at("10:30").do(job)` registers a daily job at 10:30 without raising.

In Python with only 'schedule' installed (fresh environment, no extra packages), the README usage line `schedule.every().day.at("12:42", "Europe/Amsterdam").do(job)` works, i.e. timezone-aware scheduling functions out of the box.
claims.probe_hint: python3 -m venv /tmp/vtz && /tmp/vtz/bin/pip install schedule && /tmp/vtz/bin/python -c "import schedule; schedule.every().day.at('12:42', 'Europe/Amsterdam').do(print); print('ok')"  # expect ScheduleValueError mentioning pytz if claim is false

claims.text: In Python with 'schedule' installed, `schedule.every().minute.at(":17").do(job)` registers a job for the 17th second of every minute without raising.

In Python with 'schedule' installed, `schedule.run_pending()` executes jobs that are due: a job registered with `schedule.every(1).seconds.do(f)` is invoked when run_pending() is called after more than 1 second has elapsed.
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "import schedule, time; hits=[]; schedule.every(1).seconds.do(lambda: hits.append(1)); time.sleep(1.2); schedule.run_pending(); assert hits, 'job did not run'"

claims.text: The schedule README's PyPI version badge asserts that 'schedule' is published on PyPI (latest release 1.2.2).
